newsitem.title: CHINA: SHANGHAI METAL EXCHANGE EXTENDS DELIVERY TIME.
newsitem.headline: SHANGHAI METAL EXCHANGE EXTENDS DELIVERY TIME.

text.p: The Shanghai Metal Exchange (SHME) will extend the time for physical delivery of metal futures contracts by one month, in a move traders said on Tuesday was aimed at making trade on the exchange more active.
"The extension will help the cash flow of members and customers, thus promoting trading on the exchange," a trader said.
The exchange said in a statement that the delivery time would be extended by one month from Saturday, August 16.
Members and customers could apply for delivery from the first day of the last month of trading in a maturing contract, the statement said.
Delivery currently starts after a contract matures or finishes trading on the 15th of each month, lasting from the 16th to the 20th of each month.

Shanghai traders said the move was aimed at activating trading on the SHME, which now trades futures contracts in copper, aluminium, lead, zinc, tin and nickel, with only copper and aluminium being traded in volume.
The statement said the exchange would open a window on its trading computers for physical delivery in the last month of trading of a contract.
Members and customers could apply for a delivery through the window and transactions would be done in accordance with price preferences, it said.
Unlike physical delivery in which trading ended in matured contracts when prices were settled, delivery prices in the extended period could be bargained, the statement said.
Daily price movement limits for a contract would be five percent in either direction during the extended period, against the contract's settlement price of the previous trading day, it said.
This compares with daily limits of three percent in normal futures trading.
The exchange would not add additional fees for delivery in the extended period, the statement said.
